resale_co.name: Certificate of Occupancy Transfer (Resale Application / housing inspection)
resale_co.issued_by: Pemberton Township Code Enforcement Division (Housing Code Official), Department of Community Development
resale_co.lead_time: By ordinance the Housing Officer inspects within 10 working days of a complete application with the fee. Nothing is scheduled until the application is complete and paid.
resale_co.valid_for: The application expires 60 days after it is filed and cannot be transferred. A temporary certificate for 60 days may be issued when only non-life-threatening repairs remain. How long the certificate itself is valid is not stated.
requirements: House number on the dwelling, reflective, at least 3.5 inches high and readable from the street
Fences and pool areas with self-latching, outward-swinging gates (fence at least 48 inches, latch at least 54 inches)
Landings and porches 30 inches or higher need a guard rail at least 36 inches high with openings no wider than 4 inches
Stairways, decks, porches and balconies structurally sound; handrail on any stair with 4 or more risers
No broken or missing glass; windows open, lock and have screens; egress windows open easily
Basement outside entrances kept tight against pests and water
Anti-tilt device on the stove; all utilities on at the time of inspection
Smoke alarm on every level, in every bedroom and outside each sleeping area (form says battery operated)
Carbon monoxide alarm near sleeping areas if the home has a fuel-burning appliance or attached garage
ABC fire extinguisher, 5 to 10 lb, mounted in a visible, convenient spot (April 2026 form still lists it)
Bathroom window or exhaust fan vented outside
Mechanical equipment (exhaust fans, sump pumps, wood stoves, fireplaces) safe and working
No electrical hazards: no open junction boxes, taped splices or extension-cord wiring; service wire in sound condition
GFCI protection for pools, spas, exterior and garage outlets, within 5 feet of water, and at kitchen and bath counters
Certifications may be required for roof, electrical, structural or heating items
Septic: report from a NJ licensed independent inspection company showing the septic system meets Burlington County Health Department / NJDEP standards (properties on septic)
Private well: compliance with the Private Well Testing Act; deficiencies must be fixed before transfer (properties on wells)
Public sewer or water: give the account number with the application

fees.label: Resale inspection (initial inspection)
fees.quote: A $150.00 fee must accompany the application for inspection. This fee covers the initial inspection.

fees.label: Each reinspection
fees.quote: For each subsequent reinspection, the application shall notify the Housing Code Official in writing and shall submit the reinspection fee of $50.00.

resale_co.how_to_apply: Download the Resale Application (dated 04.29.26) from the Code Enforcement/Housing Forms page. Fill it out completely and submit it with the $150 fee to the Housing Code Official's office in the Municipal Building, 500 Pemberton-Browns Mills Road (the checklist says payment goes to the cashier's office). Inspectors in the field do not accept applications or fees, and nothing is scheduled until the application is complete and paid. If the buyer is taking responsibility for the certificate, notify the office in writing before it is issued.

evidence.quote: A Certificate of Occupancy Transfer is required in the Township of Pemberton EACH time a residential dwelling unit changes occupant.
An application for inspection must be completely filled out and submitted to the Housing Code Official’s Office in the Township of Pemberton Municipal Building.
Applications are non-transferrable and will expire after 60 days.
All application and fees must be submitted to the Housing Code Officials Office. Applications and/or fees will not be accepted by the inspectors in the field.
Note: Re-inspection fee is $50. For any questions, email us at wjones@pemberton-twp.com and/or mknoblock@pemberton-twp.com.
Code Enforcement Department 500 Pemberton Browns Mills Rd Pemberton, NJ, 08015 Phone (609) 894-3376

Ashlee Bartole: 609-894-3376 (Secretary/Records Support Tech)

shall hereafter be required for human habitation of all existing dwelling units in Pemberton Township before a change in occupancy of any such unit occurs from its change in ownership or rental tenancy.
the buyer of such dwelling unit may waive the seller's responsibility and assume the same; however, that such waiver shall be in writing
make such inspections as required herein and, upon determining that the requirements have been complied with, issue a certificate of occupancy-transfer.
a temporary certificate shall be allowed to be issued for 60 days when nonlife-threatening repairs are found after the initial inspections is conducted

resale_co.notes: The township calls it a Certificate of Occupancy Transfer, required each time a dwelling changes occupant by sale or rental (Township Code Chapter 115, Ord. No. 17-2023 as amended through Ord. No. 45-2023, read through the ecode360 print view). The owner applies; the buyer may take over the duty by a written waiver filed with the Housing Officer. The ordinance and the April 29, 2026 Resale Application agree on $150 and $50 per reinspection. The Code Enforcement page now lists Wendy Jones, Ashlee Bartole (secretary, 609-894-3376), Dawn Nirdlinger and Stacy Mayle; Michael Knoblock is no longer listed there, although the April 2026 form still gives mknoblock@pemberton-twp.com as a second email. Kenneth Gerber is Director of Community Development/Zoning Official. The separate Rental Application uses the same $150 fee (rental program, not a resale item).

requirements: Smoke alarm on every level, in every bedroom and outside each sleeping area
Carbon monoxide alarm near sleeping areas (homes with a fuel-burning appliance or attached garage)
ABC fire extinguisher, 5 to 10 lb, mounted in a visible, convenient location (still on the April 2026 township checklist)

authorities.name: Not confirmed. Likely Pemberton Township Code Enforcement Division, which checks smoke alarms, CO alarms and the extinguisher under N.J.A.C. 5:70 during the Certificate of Occupancy Transfer inspection
authorities.how_to_apply: No separate smoke/CO certificate application was found. The township CO Transfer checklist covers smoke alarms, CO alarms and the extinguisher. Call Code Enforcement at 609-894-3376 to confirm whether the CO Transfer also serves as the state smoke/CO certificate.

fire_cert.notes: The NJ DCA Division of Fire Safety is listed as the fire code enforcing agency for Pemberton Township (LEA registry code S, July 2026; state directory names Fire Official Louis Kilmer, (609) 633-6132, LEA name 'Pemberton Twp Fire Prev', survey 6/16/2026). The DCA state-towns list (revised 7/17/2026) lists Pemberton Twp without the SC (smoke certs) flag, and the directory's Smoke Detector Compliance block is blank, so the state does not appear to issue smoke certificates here. Township Code Chapter 107 (Ord. No. 13-2004) still creates a Pemberton Township Bureau of Fire Prevention and lists smoke certificate fees of $35 / $70 / $125 by business days before the change of occupant, but those are the old state amounts and the DCA now shows the State as the enforcing agency, so they are not listed as current fees. Township Code §115-3C(5)(k) puts smoke alarms, CO alarms and extinguishers (inspected under N.J.A.C. 5:70) inside the CO Transfer inspection, which suggests the $150 inspection covers the smoke/CO check. The state removed the portable fire extinguisher from the sale certificate requirement in February 2025 (P.L.2025, c.19). The April 2026 township checklist still lists a 5 to 10 lb mounted ABC extinguisher.

other_items.label: Tax, water, sewer and solid waste accounts paid; liens checked
other_items.detail: The Resale Application has Tax Office and Public Works sign-off lines: liens checked, taxes paid, solid waste, water and sewer accounts paid, and sewer/water units billed.

other_items.label: Septic inspection and well testing
other_items.detail: Properties on septic must submit a report from a NJ licensed independent inspection company showing the system meets county/NJDEP standards; properties on private wells must comply with the Private Well Testing Act and fix any deficiencies before transfer. Properties on public sewer or water give the account number.

other_items.label: Open permits, code violations and vacant property fees
other_items.detail: Housing Office checks open construction permits, open code violations and vacant property registration fees before issuing.

other_items.label: Buyer assuming the certificate
other_items.detail: The buyer may take over the seller's duty to obtain the certificate with a written waiver filed with the Housing Officer before the certificate is issued.

open_questions: Who issues the state smoke/CO certificate in Pemberton Township? The state is the LEA but does not list Pemberton Twp for smoke certs, and the Township Code still names a local Bureau of Fire Prevention with old fees; confirm with Code Enforcement (609-894-3376) whether the CO Transfer covers it.
Is there a rush fee or minimum lead time before closing? None is published.
How long is the issued certificate valid? Only the 60-day application expiry is stated.
Is the extinguisher still required given P.L.2025, c.19? The April 2026 checklist and the Township Code still list it.
